title: The Pepper Tree Hollow
story:
James walked the sun-warmed southern trail with a lighter step than he had known in days, leaving the heavy, sullen air of El Pedregal far behind. Ahead of him, Nico darted through the tall amber grass, pausing every few leaps to twitch his whiskers and test the morning breeze. James checked his polished brass pocket compass, watching the slender needle point steadily southward down the expanding green valley.

James had never traveled with a companion so small, James had never heard such cheerful scampering in the brush, James had never felt quite so accompanied on an empty road. Every few paces, Nico would scramble up a dry agave stalk, look back over his shoulder with bright, inquisitive eyes, and wait for James to catch up. They moved in a quiet, companionable rhythm through the rolling foothills, where the scent of wild sage mingled with the dust of the sun-baked path.

By midday, the dirt track wound past a cluster of crumbling stone sheepfolds half-swallowed by creeping vines. Pausing beside a mossy boulder, James closed his eyes for a brief moment, counting three distinct sounds—the dry rustle of grasshoppers, the distant call of a hawk, and Nico's tiny, inquiring squeak from the stone wall. Opening his eyes to the unfamiliar vista stretching toward the southern horizon, he murmured his habitual greeting: 'Pleased to meet you, whatever comes next.'

They pressed on through the afternoon heat until the trail dipped into a shallow, shaded hollow sheltered by a sprawling pepper tree. Here, out of the wind and bathed in dappled golden light, they settled among the gnarled roots to share a moment of rest. Nico busied himself investigating a fallen twig, while James unspooled a short length of kite twine to tie back his map strap, feeling the quiet, steady pulse of a journey well underway. As the sun dipped lower, casting long amber shadows across the grass, James watched a single pale leaf drift lazily from the boughs above, wondering what nameless ridge waited just beyond the next fold of the hills.
location: Beneath a sprawling pepper tree along the southern valley trail
